title: Iki plugin (iki/v1)
description: A plugin's `plugin.yaml`: its name, what it depends on, and the settings it takes.

apiVersion.description: The spec version this manifest follows.

name.description: The plugin's name, as `namespace/name`: your lab's or company's namespace, such as `acme/assays`. Its types are `acme/assays.Type`, and its tables start with `acme__assays_`. The `iki` namespace is Iki's own.

version.description: The plugin's release, as a semantic version such as `1.4.0`. Deployments pin the git commit; this is for people.

license.description: The plugin's license, as an SPDX expression such as `Apache-2.0` or `LicenseRef-Acme-Internal`.

homepage.description: Where to read about the plugin (https only).

iki.description: The Iki releases the plugin works with, as comparisons with release numbers separated by commas, such as `>=0.1,<0.3`. A deployment on any other release refuses it. Leaving it out says nothing either way.

dependencies.description: Other plugins this one uses, by name (such as `iki/protein`), with the schema versions of their types it works with.

formats.description: File formats owned by this plugin under stable local names, such as mars-csv. A field can name the format as acme/lab.mars-csv.

starters.description: Project setup recipes shipped with this plugin, by starter ID and exact recipe version. The server offers installed recipes it supports (ADR 0198).

roles.description: The lab roles this plugin declares, such as `analyst`, `reviewer` and `qa`, by name (ADR 0116). A project's Admins give them to its members, people or teams, beside their project role, and a state field's states (ADR 0125) and a workflow step's approval can require one. Elsewhere a role is `namespace/plugin.role`, such as `acme/assays.qa`.

apis.description: The outside APIs its actions call, such as a hosted model, by name (ADR 0130). Org Admins approve each one per project, people see what's sent before they launch, and runs call it through Iki's egress proxy, which adds the organization's key and records each call.

media_types.description: The canonical media type first, followed by equivalent spellings accepted for this format.

extensions.description: Lower-case filename suffixes including the leading dot, such as .fastq.gz.

signatures.description: Alternative exact byte sequences. Each must fit within the first 4096 bytes.

hex.description: The bytes, in hex, such as `41424946` for `ABIF`.

offset.description: Where in the file the bytes start, counting from 0.

reader.description: Which of Iki's own readers takes the file's metadata, such as when it was acquired: `abif` for Sanger traces, `fcs` for flow cytometry, `mzml` for mass spectra, `czi` for Zeiss microscope images, `csv` for tables. A manifest can't supply its own.

viewer.description: The Iki viewer that shows this format's contents: on a file's page and from the records and runs that hold it (ADR 0226), and, for structure and alignment, in a type's display.viewers.

label.description: What people see, such as `QA` or `Reviewer`.

description.description: What someone with the role does, shown where Admins give it, such as `Releases reviewed samples`.

versionConstraint.description: Comparisons with whole schema versions, separated by commas, such as `>=2` or `>=2,<4`.

label.description: Its provider's name for it, as people see it, such as `FoldServe`.

host.description: The host its calls go to, over HTTPS: a name, not a domain (no `*.`). `{settings.<name>}` is the host a deployment gives in that setting, which has `format: hostname`.

purpose.description: What the plugin uses it for, as Org Admins approve it and people consent to it, such as `Predicts protein structures with FoldServe's hosted models.`

credential.description: The organization's key for it: a run secret the egress proxy adds to each call. Runs' commands never see it.

secret.description: The run secret it's kept as, for this plugin, such as `FOLDSERVE_API_KEY`.

header.description: The header it goes in. Defaults to `Authorization`.

prefix.description: What comes before it in the header. Defaults to `Bearer ` for `Authorization`, else nothing.

description.description: For the administrators who set it: what it's for, and where to get one.

reports.description: What Iki keeps of each call, for the run's provenance and cost.

model.description: The model the answer says answered.

version.description: Its version, as the answer says.

parameters.description: JSON pointers in each request's body whose values are kept, such as `/num_recycles`. Never the data itself.

jobs.description: For an API whose work is a job to submit and then poll: a run can park while it runs, holding no worker, and resume once it's done.

poll.description: Where its state is: polled with GET.

status.description: Where the poll's answer says its state.

done.description: The states that say it's done: the run resumes.

failed.description: The states that say it failed: the run fails.

message.description: Where a failed job's answer says why.

cancel.description: Where to ask it to stop, with POST, when the run is cancelled or times out.

every.description: How often to poll. Defaults to 30s; at least 5s.

timeout.description: The longest a run waits on it. Defaults to 1d; at most 7d.

usage.description: Usage the last poll's answer reports: what the job used in all.

webhook.description: When it calls back once a job is done: how its callbacks are signed. A callback that verifies makes Iki poll at once.

signature.description: `standard-webhooks` (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers), or `hmac-sha256`: the body's HMAC-SHA256 in hex, in `header`, optionally after `sha256=`.

secret.description: The run secret its callbacks are signed with.

header.description: For `hmac-sha256`: the header the signature is in.

locator.description: Where in an answer a value is: a JSON pointer in its JSON body (or, for a streamed answer, in the last event that has it), such as `/model`, or `header:<name>`.

path.description: A path on the API's host with the job's ID as `{id}`, such as `/v1/jobs/{id}`.

usage.description: Usage the answer reports, by name, such as `gpu_seconds: /usage/gpu_seconds`: numbers a deployment can price (ADR 0130).
